findings.text: blocking: _record_predates_unmarked_refusal keys the classification on the review record's own storage timestamp, and store_review stamps that field with the current moment, so from UNMARKED_SEVERITY_REFUSED_FROM (2026-10-01T07:14:36+00:00) onward every finding that lacks a severity is classified unmarked and dropped from the repair. The premise stated at repair.py:44 (the store refuses a review carrying a finding with no severity) is not enforced by store_review, which accepts an unmarked finding and stamps it now, so such a finding on a newly-stored record is not there by omission and the change silently discards a finding a reviewer did raise. Measured: the six sibling repair suites pass 39, fail 0 at the parent 16434dd94 and fail 14 at the reviewed head 1e6d4503f, including tests/test_review_findings_compose_a_repair.py::test_a_findings_review_composes_one_repair_node, the plan section 3 acceptance test that drives a three-finding stored review and asserts one repair node is composed. The brief ran only two files and left the wider population to merge, so this is the state the coordinator's merge-time gate now inherits rather than a file the node was told to run.

follow-on: UNMARKED_SEVERITY_REFUSED_FROM names a write-time refusal that is advisory rather than enforced, and the classification it feeds is duplicated in reckon/crew/reports.py, where _severity_stated judges a value outside the declared vocabulary as absent (unmarked) while repair._finding_kind judges the same value a follow-on. Each carries a fixed instant in product source that only one of them reads. Take the severity decision from the one place that already makes it (reckon/crew/reports.py _severity_stated), or enforce the refusal the constant names, so the two readers cannot disagree about which findings are unmarked.
